trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Tumakuru, M.C.No.77/2016
case_name: K.S. Vinay Kumar vs Smt. C.H. Meghana
facts_of_case: Marriage between parties was solemnized on 04.05.2012. A son was born out of wedlock. Appellant/husband filed petition seeking dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1)(ia) and (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Family court dissolved marriage on ground of desertion and awarded Rs.5 Lakhs as permanent alimony.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the appellant to establish that the order granting permanent alimony is unreasonable.
legal_principles.held: We have considered the submissions made on both sides and have perused the record. Admittedly, the applicant has not been able to demonstrate that the amount of permanent alimony awarded by the family court is unreasonable.

legal_principles.principle: The amount of permanent alimony awarded by the family court is reasonable and just.
legal_principles.held: Learned counsel for the respondent has supported the judgment and decree passed by the family court and has submitted that the amount of permanent alimony awarded by the family court is reasonable and is just and proper.

outcome.final_order: Appellant's appeal against quantum of permanent alimony was allowed.
